A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MED retrieval study. All 18 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including proofs, experimental figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. The substantial expansion does not prevent matching retained content.

before.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 1 report original centroid-embedding optimization simulations for synthetic top-2 retrieval; Appendix B supplies simulation code.

after.justification: Section 5 reports synthetic retrieval simulations and original LIMIT/LIMIT-small experiments, with numerical results in Figures 1–2 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: V3 retains centroid optimization but adds label-unaware random token-sum retrieval: shared Gaussian token vectors are summed into document/query embeddings and ranked by inner product. It also implements deterministic squared-polynomial query construction for cyclic-polytope overfitting. These add substantive retrieval procedures beyond v1's optimized centroid experiment.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates abstract synthetic top-2 subset retrieval. V3 retains that coverage and adds text-based LIMIT and LIMIT-small retrieval, introducing actual document/query tokenization and relevance evaluation rather than merely changing synthetic sample counts.

E2.justification: The WBNL fitted free-embedding reference is retained. V3 adds Promptriever Llama3 8B at dimension 4096 as the principal LIMIT comparator, using reported Recall@2 values of 0.030 and 0.543, and compares three token-sum variants. These are substantive new comparisons; the Promptriever scores are attributed to prior work rather than reported as reruns.

E3.justification: V3 adds Recall@2 evaluation with 1,000 queries per LIMIT dataset, dimensions 32–4096, and separate dimension-4 overfitting using known relevant documents. Its plotted centroid grid starts at m=10 rather than v1's m=5. The retained simulation still uses Adam and hinge loss; omission of v1's training schedule does not establish a changed training budget.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's centroid scaling analysis, v3 adds systematic tokenizer controls comparing handmade phrases, vanilla words and Qwen tokens across embedding dimensions. These test sensitivity to tokenization and available vocabulary knowledge. The separate cyclic-polytope overfit also checks whether the benchmark admits exact low-dimensional solutions.

E5.justification: V1 gives no explicit random seeds. Appendix C of v3 specifies seed 42+d for token-sum results, except seed 107 for full LIMIT vanilla at d=64. This adds seed disclosure, without establishing increased repeated runs or introducing confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive LIMIT results, including vanilla Recall@2 of 0.7060/0.9545 at d=4096 and reported cyclic-polytope Recall@2 of 1 on both datasets at d=4. Figure 1 also changes centroid dimensions from 7 to 8 at m=20 and from 23 to 24 at m=640. These are revised reported witnesses; identical optimization settings are not established.

T1.justification: V3 adds normalized RMED/RMED-C definitions, packing bounds, the sharp margin ceiling m/sqrt(k(m-1)(m-k)), robust centroid proofs, and simplex/JL constructions. Appendix A.1 strengthens exact linear MED to min{2k,m-1}. Existing Euclidean and centroid proofs are revised, while the exact centroid bounds are retained. The new JL bound in Appendix A.3 has a displayed denominator inconsistent with its proof's inverse-square margin-slack dependence.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes dimension-independent exact capacity and attributes practical limitations to learnability. V3 retains the exact Theta(k) claim but adds robust margin feasibility and LIMIT counterexamples as central contributions. Its principal geometric conclusion is narrowed to the absence of an exact-capacity obstruction, acknowledging a different normalized positive-margin regime.

C2.justification: V1 already mentions finite precision and the many required query maps. V3 adds substantive boundaries from normalized margins and conditioning, distinguishes exact witnesses from generalizing encoders, and explicitly states that its experiments do not refute positive-margin lower bounds. It also interprets the new tokenizer controls in terms of representation, feature allocation and optimization.

D1.justification: V1 includes executable simulation code with learning-rate scaling, scheduling, stopping and dimension-search details. V3 removes that listing and supplies a repository link instead. It adds token-sum pseudocode, tokenizer identification, observed-vocabulary allocation, repeated-token and chunking details, plus exported document/query vectors. The PDFs therefore gain new implementation information while losing self-contained simulation details.

R1.justification: V3 substantially revises its relationship to Weller's work by recognizing compatibility with positive-margin bounds. Section 6 and Appendix B replace v1's direct bound comparisons to Guo and hierarchical retrieval with qualified comparisons between different structured settings. Alon and Vershynin are added and Hornik is removed; Weller's publication update alone is not counted as a new work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, discussions, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V1's combined centroid-theory/simulation section becomes separate robust-theory and experimental sections. Appendices are reorganized into expanded proofs, theoretical comparisons, retrieval algorithms/results and embedding tables. These are substantial narrative changes beyond inserting new scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column conference formatting. Figure 1's two panels become one redesigned plot with a cyclic-polytope series and witness terminology. V3 adds Figure 2, five experimental/vector tables and an algorithm display, while removing v1's theoretical summary table and long code listing; the summary table's mathematical content remains elsewhere.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially improves the central argument by separating exact capacity from normalized-margin feasibility, strengthening the exact linear bound, revising proofs and correcting comparisons with structured retrieval theory. The tokenizer controls add evidence relevant to its narrowed empirical claim. These gains address important scope and rigor weaknesses in v1. They outweigh the loss of inline simulation code and the localized but substantive inconsistency between Appendix A.3's JL bound and its derivation.
